newsitem.title: USA: IMF approves $47 mln Armenia loan, challenges ahead.
newsitem.headline: IMF approves $47 mln Armenia loan, challenges ahead.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund on Tuesday approved a $47 million loan to the former Soviet republic of Armenia, but said the tax situation was fragile and Yerevan needed to build up currency reserves.
An IMF statement said the loan would be released in two tranches, and the first tranche could be drawn on June 30.
"Although good macro-economic performance in 1997 is within reach, the fiscal situation remains fragile and external sustainability could become an issue over the medium term," it said.

"The authorities will therefore need to consolidate the fiscal gains achieved so far, restore confidence in the dram (currency) and accumulate a reasonable cushion of reserves to weather external shocks," it said.
The IMF programme envisages Armenian GDP growth of 5.8 percent this year after 5.8 percent in 1996, and it projects a rise to 6.0 percent in 1998 and 1999.
Inflation is set to rise to 9.5 percent this year, from 5.7 percent in 1996, but it will fall to 8.0 percent in 1998 and to 6.2 percent in 1999.
